subject: Biology
description: Mendel, DNA/RNA, blood groups, sex determination, basic genetic disorders

questions.explanation: Mendel (1822-1884), an Austrian monk, worked with pea plants (Pisum sativum) and derived the laws of segregation and independent assortment (1866). His work was rediscovered c. 1900 and became the foundation of classical genetics.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The number of chromosomes in a NORMAL HUMAN SOMATIC (body) cell is:
questions.explanation: Humans are diploid with 23 pairs = 46 chromosomes. 22 autosomal pairs + 1 sex chromosome pair (XX female / XY male). Gametes (sperm/ovum) are haploid with 23 chromosomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: In humans, the SEX of the child is determined by:

options.option_text: Whether the sperm carries an X or Y chromosome

questions.explanation: Mother is XX — all ova carry X. Father is XY — half of sperm carry X (→ daughter XX) and half carry Y (→ son XY). So the father's sperm determines the child's sex, not the mother.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The UNIVERSAL DONOR blood group is:
questions.explanation: O-negative red cells lack A, B, and Rh(D) antigens, so no recipient will immediately attack them. Hence O− is the universal RBC donor. AB+ is the universal RBC RECIPIENT (no antibodies against any antigen). For plasma, AB is the universal donor.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about DNA. 1. Its double-helix structure was proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953. 2. Adenine pairs with Thymine via 2 hydrogen bonds; Guanine pairs with Cytosine via 3 hydrogen bonds. 3. Sugar in DNA is deoxyribose; in RNA it is ribose. 4. DNA stores genetic information; RNA primarily carries it out during protein synthesis. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Rosalind Franklin's X-ray diffraction images (Photo 51) were crucial to the 1953 model. A-T (2 H-bonds), G-C (3 H-bonds) is why GC-rich regions are more thermally stable. mRNA, tRNA and rRNA mediate protein synthesis from the DNA blueprint.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the GENETIC / CHROMOSOMAL DISORDER with its cause. A. Down syndrome. B. Turner syndrome. C. Klinefelter syndrome. D. Sickle-cell anaemia. List-II: 1. Trisomy 21 (extra chromosome 21). 2. 45, X — one X missing in females. 3. 47, XXY — extra X in males. 4. Point mutation in the β-globin gene.
questions.explanation: Down = trisomy 21 (the most common viable autosomal trisomy). Turner = 45, X (one sex chromosome missing; affects females). Klinefelter = 47, XXY (affects males, often infertile). Sickle-cell = autosomal recessive point mutation (Glu → Val at β-6).
